subject: owl
pitch: A great horned owl perched on a gnarled branch. Mottled bark-brown and buff feathers with fine dark barring, a pale bib at the throat, tall feathered ear tufts, a round tawny facial disc rimmed in black, huge orange eyes and a hooked grey beak. Feathered legs end in strong black talons gripping the wood.
reasoning:
I'm planning the owl's skeleton structure—spine, neck, head, jaw, wing chains, tail, and legs with toes—plus a branch prop, aiming for a great horned owl roughly 0.55m tall perched upright with slight tilt, and working out the coordinate system for positioning it on the branch.

Still defining joint positions...

Each toe gets a short two-joint chain off the ankle, swept into capsule shapes. For the body, I'm sculpting an ellipsoid with mottled brown/buff feather barring, countershading the belly with striped buff tones against a darker mottled back, and adding a pale bib ellipsoid at the throat.

For the head, I'm shaping a flattened sphere with facial discs made from scaled, slightly rotated flat spheres in tawny with dark rims behind them, plus orange eye spheres with black forward-set pupils and dark brow accents.

Now I'm figuring out the beak using angled cones for the hooked upper and smaller lower parts, positioning tufted ear cones leaning outward in dark brown and buff tones.

For the wings, I'm sketching a chain of joints from shoulder to elbow to wrist, then considering whether to loft a flattened sweep along those points or simply use scaled ellipsoid parts per bone for a flatter, simpler wing shape.

Still defining tail geometry and skeleton joints...

Still defining limb joints...

Working out toe placement on the branch...

Still writing branch path...

Adding a twig spike up to the bark with a knot, then setting up bark and feather paints using mottled and grain textures combined with countershading and stripe patterns for the body.

Blending chest and back colors by resolving each paint's RGB at that point and mixing based on the z-facing smoothstep, using the exported mix/resolve/smoothstep helpers. Now I'm moving on to the wing coloring, using mottled stripes for the dark brown and tan pattern.

For the head, I'm applying a tawny mottle and placing a facial disc (tawny with a dark rim) as a flattened sphere positioned and scaled against the head ellipsoid geometry, working out coordinates so it sits correctly on the face.

I'm positioning the eyes as orange spheres with black pupils offset slightly forward, and starting on a dark brow box positioned above them with a slight rotation.

For the brow rotation, I'm working out the sign convention so the inner end (closer to center) tilts lower and the outer end tilts higher, giving an angry expression -- mirrored for each side based on which side of center it's on.

Now I'm setting up a beak using a cone shape positioned between the eyes, angling it downward and forward from center.

Still working out positioning... I'm adding a smaller hooked lower beak cone on the jaw, plus a buff-colored feathered chin lump nearby, then starting on ear tufts as small angled cones near the sides of the head.

For the ear tufts I'm shaping dark cones with painted buff-tipped stripes, then moving on to a pale bib sphere at the throat and assigning explicit bones (head, spine1) to each piece so they track skeletal motion properly. I'm also considering scalloped feather layers for the shoulder/back ruff area.

Positioning chest feathers...

I'll skip adding back feathers since the paint color handles that visual continuity, and I'm noting the belly should stay pale underneath. Now I'm thinking about the tail fan structure, placing feather joints along the tail chain.

Still writing feather positions...

Still defining wing geometry...

Adding more body parts...

Now I'm setting up the skeleton chains — spine, neck, and tail each as parented joint sequences with defined paths, with tails branching from the hips and feathers attached to the tail bones.

For the facial disc coloring I'm mottling a tawny pattern with a dark rim, then mirroring the geometry across the x-axis for symmetry. I'm checking the toe placement against the branch surface geometry, calculating the branch's curved surface height at each toe's z-position to make sure the toes sit flush on top rather than floating above it.

Adding talon spikes with rounded cap ends and double-checking the ankle joint position, then finalizing the mesh export and returning the root node.
